### Is this a new bug in dbt-redshift?

- [X] I believe this is a new bug in dbt-redshift
- [X] I have searched the existing issues, and I could not find an existing issue for this bug

### Current Behavior

When the dbt Cloud connection is set to database "development" and your `dbt_project.yml` file states all model nodes occur in database `sources` then `dbt compile` and `dbt build` will not work. 

### Expected Behavior

The database specified in `dbt_project.yml` for a model is used as specified. At the least, when using RA3 nodes and a database user that has permissions, dbt should be able to run `dbt compile` successfully regardless of the database specified in the Connection.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Have a Redshift cluster with RA3 nodes. Have a database connection to database A. Have a Redshift db user with, at least, database permissions to database A and B. Have a `dbt_project.yml` file that specifies `+database: B`.
2. Run `dbt compile`.
3. Receive error message.

### Relevant log output

```shell
22:19:23  Began running node model.redshift_us_east_1.clean_table_coconut
22:19:23  Re-using an available connection from the pool (formerly list_sources_dbt_developer_contracts, now model.redshift_us_east_1.clean_table_coconut)
22:19:23  Began compiling node model.redshift_us_east_1.clean_table_coconut
22:19:23  Using redshift connection "model.redshift_us_east_1.clean_table_coconut"
22:19:23  On model.redshift_us_east_1.clean_table_coconut: BEGIN
22:19:23  Opening a new connection, currently in state closed
22:19:23  Redshift adapter: Establishing connection using ssl with `sslmode` set to 'prefer'.To connect without ssl, set `sslmode` to 'disable'.
22:19:23  Redshift adapter: Connecting to redshift with username/password based auth...
22:19:23  SQL status: SUCCESS in 0.0 seconds
22:19:23  Using redshift connection "model.redshift_us_east_1.clean_table_coconut"
22:19:23  On model.redshift_us_east_1.clean_table_coconut: /* {"app": "dbt", "dbt_version": "1.5.9", "profile_name": "user", "target_name": "default", "node_id": "model.redshift_us_east_1.clean_table_coconut"} */
SELECT *
    FROM sources.information_schema.tables 
    WHERE table_name = 'clean_table_coconut' and table_schema = 'dbt_developer_transforms'
22:19:23  Redshift adapter: Redshift error: Only user perm tables supported in producer views
22:19:23  On model.redshift_us_east_1.clean_table_coconut: ROLLBACK
22:19:23  Timing info for model.redshift_us_east_1.clean_table_coconut (compile): 22:19:23.485015 => 22:19:23.666072
22:19:23  On model.redshift_us_east_1.clean_table_coconut: Close
22:19:23  Database Error in model clean_table_coconut (models/upstream_prepared/sqlserverdbname_dbo/clean_table_coconut.sql)
  Only user perm tables supported in producer views
22:19:23  Finished running node model.redshift_us_east_1.clean_table_coconut
```


### Environment

```markdown
- OS: dbt Cloud
- Python: dbt Cloud
- dbt-core: 1.5
- dbt-redshift: dbt Cloud
```


### Additional Context

Why can't I just change the database name in the dbt Cloud Connection to be correct? Because that will generate a new ssh key set which means the public_key has to get PRed by DevOps into the right place which will take an unspecified amount of time. (So yes, I'm going to go through that process, but also it would be great for this to be fixed so someone else doesn't have to deal with it. Also, supporting RA3 nodes in general.)

Why? Well it's **_not_** any of these:
A) user permissions. The `Only user perm tables supported in producer views` in the error message implies it's a permission issue. So I explicitly permissioned the user account for allllll the things - `usage`, `select`, `all` `alter default privileges` on `tables`, `schema` and added it to groups with at least `SELECT` permissions on the same. No go. This database user also created and owns the database it's referencing and all the objects it's trying to read information about. In addition, the database user in my dbt Cloud profile settings is a superuser. (Technically, it doesn't own this particular schema.)
B) It occurred to me that the dbt-redshift adapter should be doing something like `USE DATABASE sources`  but a) Redshift doesn't seem to have the `USE` keyword from a web search and b) dbt is correctly writing the database name `sources` in the query it runs against the `information_schema`.
C) Maybe it was that Redshift doesn't support cross-database work - unless you use RA3 nodes and then it supports `SELECT`s. These are RA3 nodes, so it should be able to run a `SELECT` on the `sources` database `information_schema` schema. 
D) The database connection just doesn't work. Incorrect. i) `dbt seed` runs fine and creates 3 tables, albeit in the wrong place - database apple. This is expected - RA3 nodes don't support writes. (Specifying database B for seed writes also results, as expected, in an error.) ii)There's a SUCCESS message for the connection in the log.
E) Fluke one off. No, this happened multiple times.
G) Something about whether an object exists or not. I received the error whether the object I was trying to refresh already existed or didn't(deleted manually outside of dbt).

You can possibly argue what the bug is/bugs are, but something doesn't work correctly. Possible interpretations of this bug are:

1. Redshift itself has a problem. 
2. dbt-core is missing some code/syntax around supporting RA3 nodes and/or cross-database reads.
3. dbt-core could return a better error message.
4. dbt Cloud Connection page could have a warning about what database name you put in.
5. User error. I'm completely missing something. 
6. Something else.

items.body:
### Describe the feature request.

## Azure SDP Integration – Summary and Requirements

This work is tracked in the following GitHub issues:
- [create-a-derived-table #2767](https://github.com/moj-analytical-services/create-a-derived-table/issues/2767)
- [dmet-hmcts #78](https://github.com/moj-analytical-services/dmet-hmcts/issues/78)

### Core Requirements

We have two primary technical requirements (outlined in more detail in the tickets above):

- The ability to execute `dbt` models sourced from [CaDT](https://github.com/moj-analytical-services/create-a-derived-table) on a dedicated SQL pool hosted in Azure SDP.
- A lambda that allows for federated queries across the network from AWS Athena to the SDP SQL pools. We have agreed that this can be created using a lambda, if that's the simplest and best solution given the timeframes.

The ability to run `dbt` on the SDP is the immediate priority. Completing this will enable us to formally begin trialling OneCrown workflows on a new cloud-native architecture.

We are aiming to have this work completed by the end of April.

---

### Additional Requirements

Beyond our core requirements, there are a few additional areas we are keen to explore:

- As discussed with Jacob HP, we are interested in the potential for translating SQL models between dialects within `dbt`. If this is not feasible, future One X projects will need to manually convert models to the required format. A summary of our own investigation into this can be found [here](https://github.com/moj-analytical-services/create-a-derived-table/issues/3216).
- The ability for users to request service principal access to specific datasets within SDP, using their existing alpha users. Ideally, Analytical Platform (AP) users would be able to query the SDP directly from within their existing AP-hosted IDEs, using the same `dbt` workflows, with only the profile needing to change to target the SDP.

These items are considered lower priority and can be picked up after April, depending on resource availability within AP.

---

### Longer-Term Considerations

Initially, we plan to use the [`dbt-synapse`](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/core/connect-data-platform/azuresynapse-setup) adapter to support the execution of models on the dedicated SQL pool. However, this approach is costly, as the pool will often sit idle outside of scheduled dbt runs.

In the longer term, we would like to move to a serverless solution on the SDP. The HMCTS team plans to trial Azure Fabric, which would allow us to transition to using [`dbt-fabric`](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/core/connect-data-platform/fabric-setup), reducing infrastructure costs and complexity. When the time comes, we are keen to explore migrating to this new setup.

---

### Implementation Overview (from Gustav)

> The following steps outline the key technical actions required to enable the proposed solution for OneCrown:

1. **Provision a dedicated pool in SDP**, replicating the networking and authentication setup intended for production.  
   *Key contacts: Qiang Zhou, Zain Zafar (SDP)*

2. **Establish network connectivity** between MoJ infrastructure and SDP via the existing site-to-site VPN.  
   GitHub Actions must be able to deploy models to SDP across this connection.  
   *Key contacts: Julia Lawrence, Jacob Woffenden, Jacob HP*

3. **Create a new service principal** with appropriate read and write permissions to access the dedicated pool.  
   *Key contacts: Qiang Zhou, Zain Zafar, HMCTS PlatOps*

4. **Store the service principal credentials securely** in AWS infrastructure, and configure GitHub Actions to use them.  
   *Key contacts: Julia Lawrence, Jacob Woffenden, Jacob HP*

5. **Validate the setup using dummy data**, such as the Jaffle Shop example or a more complex dbt project.  
   *Key contact: Tom Hepworth*

---

### Execution Requirements for dbt

To support dbt execution on our self-hosted runners, the following system dependencies must be installed:

- `unixODBC`
- `msodbcsql18` (Microsoft ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server)

---

### Supporting Documentation

For further context and guidance, please refer to:

- [How to Connect AP Athena to a Dedicated SQL Pool in Azure Synapse (PDF)](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19689056/CDE1-How.to.Connect.AP.Athena.to.a.Dedicated.SQL.Pool.in.Azure.Synapse-100425-170124.pdf)
- [How to Connect CaDT to a Dedicated SQL Pool in Azure Synapse (PDF)](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19689057/CDE1-How.to.Connect.CaDT.to.a.Dedicated.SQL.Pool.in.Azure.Synapse-100425-170118.pdf)

---

### Contacts

#### MoJ Data Engineering

- [Thomas Hepworth](thomas.hepworth@justice.gov.uk) (Data Engineer): Main contact on the Data Engineering side
- [Oliver Critchfield](Oliver.Critchfield@justice.gov.uk) (Data Engineer)

#### HMCTS

- [Qiang Zhou](Qiang.Zhou@HMCTS.NET) (Developer): Main contact on the HMCTS side until May
- [Siby George](Siby.George@justice.gov.uk) (Developer): New lead on the HMCTS side of this

### Describe the context.

This work is a core part of the OneCrown project, which is looking to build a single, consistent, and flexible dataset that can meet both HMCTS and MoJ requirements for management information, reporting, modelling, forecasting and analysis.

This infrastructure will allow data transfer between the two organisations and should simplify our workflows significantly.

### Value / Purpose

This work will significantly reduce the duplication of effort currently seen across HMCTS and MoJ, and will also lay the groundwork for deeper cross-departmental collaboration in the future.

In the longer term, it is expected to support greater trust and confidence in our published figures.

### User Types

Anyone working with criminal courts data from across MoJ and HMCTS

[Bug] High-concurrency run with threads: 4 acquires a sixth REPL during after-run and starts a second Livy session
items.body:
### Is this a new bug?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug
- [x] I have searched the existing issues, and I could not find an existing issue for this bug

### Current Behavior

With `high_concurrency: true`, `threads: 4`, and Fabric's default limit of five
REPLs per underlying Livy session, one `dbt run` acquires six HC session
IDs/REPLs and starts a second physical Livy session.

The project sets `flags.populate_cache: false`. Therefore, eager relation-cache
population is disabled and before-run does not fan metadata listing out over
multiple worker connections. Only one master REPL is acquired before model
execution. This makes the observed lifecycle unambiguous:

1. Before-run/main acquires one HC ID/REPL for Spark/version and schema
   preparation.
2. Four dbt worker threads acquire four additional HC IDs/REPLs.
3. These five REPLs are packed into the first physical Livy session.
4. All eleven models finish and the worker statements are no longer active.
5. MainThread opens a new connection for after-run and acquires a sixth HC
   ID/REPL instead of reusing a no-longer-active REPL from the same process.
6. Because the first physical session already contains five REPLs, Fabric puts
   the sixth REPL on a second physical Livy session.

`populate_cache: false` does not cause the lifecycle defect. It only ensures
that metadata fan-out does not obscure the count. The extra acquisition occurs
because a completed connection's HC REPL is not exposed as a reusable resource
for a later dbt phase.

The models complete successfully, but the unnecessary physical session adds a
second Spark startup, extra capacity usage/cost, and session churn. In the
captured run, the last model finished at `15:34:07`; the sixth REPL did not
become ready until `15:34:51`, approximately 44 seconds later.

### Expected Behavior

With `threads: 4` and the default five-REPL cap, the complete dbt invocation
should remain on one physical Livy session:

- one REPL may serve the main/master connection;
- up to four REPLs may be leased by worker connections;
- when a connection closes and its statement is no longer active, its healthy
  REPL should be reusable by a later connection in the same dbt process;
- after-run/on-run-end should borrow an idle REPL instead of acquiring a sixth
  HC session ID.

The adapter should preserve exclusive access while a REPL is leased, and it
should delete/re-acquire a REPL if that REPL is dead or stale.

This expectation is consistent with the adapter README, which states that one
build holds up to `threads + 1` REPLs and that `threads <= 4` fits into one
physical Livy session when the default cap is five.


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install `dbt-core 1.11.12`, `dbt-adapters 1.24.2`, and
   `dbt-fabricspark 1.12.9` in a clean/unmodified environment.
2. Configure the Fabric Lakehouse output with:

   ```yaml
   threads: 4
   high_concurrency: true
   reuse_session: true
   spark_config:
     name: <application-name>
     artifactName: <lakehouse-name>
   ```

   Do not override `spark.highConcurrency.max`; leave the cap at its default of
   five.

3. Disable eager relation-cache population in `dbt_project.yml`:

   ```yaml
   flags:
     populate_cache: false
   ```

4. Run a DAG that has at least four concurrently runnable models so all four
   dbt worker threads open HC connections. In the observed case, the command
   was:

   ```text
   dbt run --select tag:snop_silver
   ```

   It selected nine table models and two incremental models.

5. Inspect `dbt.log` and Fabric Monitoring Hub.
6. Observe one before-run/master HC ID followed by four worker HC IDs. All five
   REPLs use the same underlying `sessionId`.
7. After the eleventh model finishes, observe MainThread open a new connection
   and acquire a sixth HC ID.
8. Observe that the sixth REPL has a different underlying `sessionId`, while
   Monitoring Hub shows a second physical Livy session for the same dbt run.

### Relevant log output

```shell
Running with dbt=1.11.12
Registered adapter: fabricspark=1.12.9
Concurrency: 4 threads

15:31:18 [before-run/master]
HC session ready: hc_id=<hc-main>
sessionId=<physical-session-A> replId=<repl-main>

15:31:40 [four dbt workers]
HC session ready: hc_id=<hc-worker-1>
sessionId=<physical-session-A> replId=<repl-1>
HC session ready: hc_id=<hc-worker-2>
sessionId=<physical-session-A> replId=<repl-2>
HC session ready: hc_id=<hc-worker-3>
sessionId=<physical-session-A> replId=<repl-3>
HC session ready: hc_id=<hc-worker-4>
sessionId=<physical-session-A> replId=<repl-4>

15:34:07 [model phase]
11 of 11 OK created sql table model <redacted-model>
Finished running node <redacted-model>

15:34:07 [MainThread/after-run]
Opening a new connection, currently in state init
Acquiring HC session (sessionTag=<redacted-stable-session-tag>)

15:34:51 [MainThread/after-run]
HC session ready: hc_id=<hc-after-run>
sessionId=<physical-session-B> replId=<repl-after-run>

Finished running 2 incremental models, 9 table models in 259.36s
Done. PASS=11 WARN=0 ERROR=0 SKIP=0 NO-OP=0 TOTAL=11
```

### Environment

```markdown
- OS: Microsoft Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200 (Build 26200)
- Python: 3.11.15
- dbt-adapters: 1.24.2
- dbt-fabricspark: 1.12.9
- dbt-core: 1.11.12
```

### Additional Context

#### Why this appears different from existing issues

The issue titled [High concurrency sessions are not kept alive with
`reuse_session` and
`session_idle_timeout`](https://github.com/microsoft/dbt-fabricspark/issues/232)
reported that deleting the final HC ID stopped a physical session before its
configured idle timeout could apply. The `1.12.8` fix retained HC IDs when warm
reuse was requested. That issue concerns retaining a physical session between
separate dbt invocations. This report concerns acquiring an unnecessary HC ID
inside one invocation.

The issue titled [Fabric Livy sessions always fall back to on-demand because
`spark.livy.session.idle.timeout` is
sent](https://github.com/microsoft/dbt-fabricspark/issues/184) concerns Starter
Pool configuration matching during physical-session creation. It does not
concern how many HC IDs/REPLs dbt acquires across its before-run, worker, and
after-run phases.

#### Proof-of-concept result

I tested a process-local, bounded REPL pool as a local proof of concept:

- each dbt connection exclusively borrows one healthy REPL;
- closing/releasing the connection returns the REPL to an idle pool;
- a new REPL is acquired only when no idle REPL is available and local capacity
  remains;
- stale/dead REPLs are deleted instead of reused;
- after-run borrows an existing idle REPL.

For the same eleven-model workload:

| Result | Unmodified adapter | Local POC |
|---|---:|---:|
| HC IDs/REPLs created | 6 | 4 |
| Physical Livy sessions | 2 | 1 |
| dbt models passed | 11/11 | 11/11 |

With prompt cleanup enabled, all four HC IDs owned by the POC run were also
released successfully at the end with HTTP 200.

The POC demonstrates that in-process reuse avoids the extra session; it is not
intended to prescribe the final implementation.

#### Core POC lifecycle changes

In `src/dbt/adapters/fabricspark/connections.py`, connection release was changed
from a no-op so that close reaches the HC wrapper:

```diff
 def release(self) -> None:
-    pass
+    super().release()
```

In `src/dbt/adapters/fabricspark/concurrent_livy.py`, the POC added:

```python
class HighConcurrencyReplPool:
    def __init__(self, max_size=5):
        self.max_size = max_size
        self._condition = threading.Condition()
        self._idle = []
        self._leased = set()
        self._creating = 0

    # borrow(): reuse an idle healthy REPL, otherwise acquire within capacity
    # release(): move a healthy REPL from leased back to idle
```

`HighConcurrencyConnection.close()` invokes a release callback:

```python
def close(self) -> None:
    if self._closed:
        return
    self._cursor.close()
    self._closed = True
    self._release_callback(self.hc_session)
```

`HighConcurrencySessionManager.connect()` borrows from the compatible
process-local pool instead of always constructing and acquiring a new HC
session:

```python
self._pool = _get_repl_pool(credentials)
self._hc_session = self._pool.borrow(credentials)
```

#### Multi-caller lifecycle note

If physical-session sharing across multiple dbt callers is supported, each
caller should delete only the HC IDs it acquired. It should never delete all HC
IDs belonging to the shared physical Livy session. Stable session packing and
cleanup of caller-owned HC IDs should be treated as separate lifecycle
concerns.
[POC_Result.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31540649/POC_Result.pdf)

items.title: Build a dbt adapter over the FlightSQL edge (dbt-quack)
items.body:
Follow-up to #8. That issue assumed a `dbt-flightsql` adapter to verify; no such package exists (`dbt-flightsql`/`dbt-flight`/`dbt-adbc`/`dbt-arrow-flight` all 404 on PyPI). `examples/dbt/` now verifies the FlightSQL wire end-to-end (10/10) and documents what an adapter must do. This issue tracks building the reusable adapter.

**Goal**
A dbt adapter (`dbt-quack` / `dbt-flightsql`) that lets `dbt run` / `dbt test` run natively against the quack-on-demand FlightSQL edge, consuming the `examples/dbt/profiles.yml` shape (`type: flightsql`, host/port/tenant/pool/user/password/tls).

**Base it on the Arrow ADBC FlightSQL driver** (`adbc_driver_flightsql`). It already works against the edge (see `scripts/adbc.sh` and `examples/dbt/verify.py`): Basic auth, TLS skip-verify, and `tenant`/`pool` routing headers (forwarded on every RPC including the handshake) all work out of the box. Do NOT base it on `flightsql-dbapi` (InfluxData), which omits routing headers on the Basic-auth handshake and whose `execute_update()` deadlocks against the edge.

**Edge behaviors the adapter must handle (confirmed live, see `examples/dbt/RUN_REPORT.md` and `EdgeClient` in `verify.py`)**
1. **Statements execute on `do_get`** (fetch), not at prepare. The adapter must pull the result of `CREATE`/`INSERT`/`DROP` to actually run them. ACL denials surface earlier, at prepare.
2. **Update-count statements report `inconsistent schema`.** `DROP`/`INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` advertise a `Count` FlightInfo schema but return an empty stream; ADBC raises `inconsistent schema` even though the statement ran. Treat that one case as benign (or fix the edge to return a matching stream).
3. **Fully-qualify relations under ACL.** With `acl.enabled=true`, bare names qualify against the global default catalog/schema (`qod`/`main`), not the pool's tenant-db, so per-table grants miss. The adapter should emit `catalog.schema.table` (or we expose an ACL default catalog/schema = tenant-db).

**Acceptance**
- `dbt run` + `dbt test` succeed against the edge using the `examples/dbt/` project.
- The adapter wraps the ADBC FlightSQL driver (the `EdgeClient` in `examples/dbt/verify.py` is a working reference for the connection + execute semantics).
- Replace `verify.py` in `examples/dbt/` with a real `dbt` invocation (keep `verify.py` as a wire smoke-test if useful).
- Optional: contribute the two edge-side niceties upstream/edge-side (DoPut update-result schema; ACL default catalog/schema) so the adapter needs fewer special cases.

# The tortoise path — **four stages, in this order** (owner, 2026-11-09)

**Owner ruling, verbatim:** *"1. get to private beta (so all the issues needed for that, also ensuring they're labelled p0 or p1 so the auto dispatch prioritises them) 2. any issues and work needed for the venture studio design partner (they record meetings and feed it to an extractor that needs to work for meeting transcripts…) 3. complete any remaining issues that will improve longmem eval directly … so that means also making sure they're marked in the tracking issue as the next wave(s) following private-beta ones 4. run benchmarks for longmemeeval and also for reasoning (the gbrain ones we already setup)"*

**And the ordering constraint that governs stage 4:** *"the issues we filed that affect longmem eval need to be finished before the benchmark, as otherwise we're benchmarking over something that we know is broken and know how it's broken and just needs a fix from us."*

**So: wave 3 gates wave 4.** The benchmark is a *measurement of a known-good state*, not a way to discover the state.

---

## ⛔ STAGE 1 — PRIVATE BETA: the set, stated so it can be counted

The beta is the P0/P1 set. **Re-measured 2026-11-13 by label: P0 6 · P1 23 = 29 open** (this line previously read *P0 10 · P1 17 = 27*; the P0 half was 4 CLOSED issues and the P1 half was short). Each is either *beta work*, *a decision waiting on the owner*, or *mis-filed into the wrong wave* — the table says which.

### P0 — 6 open
| issue | what it actually is | wave |
|---|---|---|
| `#5087` | **epic** Extractor v4, the selective write path (S0→S6) — 19/27 children closed | 1 (children) |
| `#5095` | **lane** L3 extractor pipeline body — 3 of its 4 issues closed, the fourth's PR landed | 1 → **verify + close** |
| `#7879` | **epic** the Postgres record — 23/36 children closed | 1 (children) |
| `#7949` | **epic** v4 CAPSTONE, the end-to-end proof (E1–E6) — 3/12 children closed | 1 |
| `#10977` | tracking: making the hosted graph usable — "the three things nobody owns" | 1 |
| `#11609` | **the live surface is 72 tools / 150 methods against an approved 27 / 40** | 1 |
| `#12047` | **P0 NEW — entity resolution does not exist and the queue reports a false clean.** `list_dedup_candidates(candidate_type='entity')` returns `[]` from a hard-coded stub, so "are there duplicate entities?" answers **none** when the truth is **cannot answer**; `#783` was closed COMPLETED on an acceptance criterion naming `entity_resolver.py`, a file that has never existed in git. Measured damage: one person under five Subject names, one role under three, documents filed as roles, `holdsRole` has zero edges in both hosted graphs, and `default`'s 872 Subjects are 870× kind `other` (453 of them `issue:<repo>#<n>`). **Blocks the graph re-file** — that work multiplies entities on every item | 1 |
| `#12477` | **P0 NEW — the hosted API times out on every request while its health check reports 2/2 passing.** Measured 2026-11-13: `GET /v1/health` / 1-row `GET /v1/points` / `POST /v1/objects` all time out (30-45 s), MCP returns `-32009 wait budget exceeded`, an in-process write hung past 300 s — while the control plane answers instantly and `flyctl` reports `2/2 checks passing` on a `shared-cpu-2x:4096MB` box that restarted at 17:53Z, with vector/FTS queries blowing a 500 ms budget at 1.5-3.9 s. **Blocks the private-beta dogfood** — the clean-graph migration cannot start until a write completes | 1 |

> **📌 Board edit 2026-11-11** — added `#11089` (P1, the `#5090` capstone) and `#4333` (P2, deliberately out of the beta set) to this table, and refreshed the `#5090` row. **The counts in this section are a MEASUREMENT STAMP, not a live figure** — they were measured by another lane on 2026-11-11 and several rows have since closed; re-measure before quoting them.

### P1 — 23 open, split by what they are *for*
| issue | subject | wave |
|---|---|---|
| `#5333` | design(extractor): the destructive half of G5 — may any pass remove/archive an existing fact? **DECIDED, needs the capstone** | 1 |
| `#10360` | extractor: no mechanical enforcement of the verbatim state-value guarantee | 1 |
| `#11002` | extractor: the eight steps actually — bounded re-narrate, S4 gap-filling misplaced. ⚠️ **Its blocker is now cleared:** the ADD-capable stage landed (`#11534` → `#11554`), which is exactly the successor S4's removal requires. The owner question was **withdrawn** 2026-11-07 — the repo's own ordering obligation decides it (build the successor, prove the merge property, then delete `run_s4`) | 1 |
| ✅ **`#11237` — LANDED 2026-11-10 (`#11548`)** | extractor: the relations channel's **write path**. It also **closed the wiring gap** I reported on 2026-11-07: `tortoise/relation_write.py` now calls `plan_hierarchy_edges` (`:53`, `:589`, `:631`) and writes the pack-declared structural hierarchy edges, so a capture **can** produce them. `#11001`'s "no production call site" finding is **false on today's main** and was corrected there and here | 1 |
| ✅ **`#11083` — CLOSED 2026-11-10** | packs: per-pack relation census + the ruled vocabulary. **Landed via `#11543`** (census artifact + `tools/pack_relation_census.py` on `main`) and the pm relations resolved (`blocks`+`dependsOn`+`direction: "<-"`, `partOfSprint`+`hasPart`, `assignedTo`+`managedBy`, `onBoard` kept as `declarationOnly` with the view reason). `funds` stayed a **label**; `produces` became a **meaning** (`<-`, IMPL) because a direction has to be recorded. ⚠️ **One residual, owed and NOT done:** `E6` is still not registered in `docs/evidence/7949-capstone/PRE-REGISTRATION.md` — the sixth acceptance row has no bar yet | 1 |
| `#11534` | extractor: the ADD-capable stage must reach PARTIAL gaps | 1 |
| `#11673` | **register `E6`** — the sixth capstone row the owner created on 2026-11-05 has no bar in `PRE-REGISTRATION.md`. ⚠️ Not a doc edit: `REQUIRED_CRITERIA` in `tools/capstone_preregistration_check.py` must gain `E6` in the same change, and the registration commit must be strictly older than any scored log. Bar proposed: **unbound-and-unexplained declared relations = 0**, denominator 42 (36 relations + 6 hierarchy paths), with the `written` column *reported beside* — not the bar, because `A1` already measures the written graph | 1 | ✅ **implemented in PR #11688** (head `41550c65a9`, MERGEABLE): `E6` is required for the **record** (`REQUIRED_CRITERIA`), recognised by the scorer (`RECOGNISED_CRITERIA`), and **not** part of the close — `V9`/`--require-green` stays `E1..E5`, per the `A1`–`A5` precedent (*"a registration may not turn a row into a gate before anyone has measured it"*). ⚠️ **The head's checks are mostly `cancelled`** (a push landed while CI was running, which cancels the queue position) — it needs a **fresh run** before the rail will accept it |
| `#11695` | **nothing can emit an `E6` verdict**, so no **scored run can produce a complete record** (`E6` is required by `REQUIRED_CRITERIA`). ⚠️ **Not** a closing blocker: the close is five rows. The fix is a producer reading the existing `docs/evidence/11083/pack-relation-census.json` — it must **not** re-open the closing set | 1 |
| `#11000` | packs: **`subclassOf` never widens — the expansion loop drops the parent** | 1 (**a pack that cannot widen connects nothing**) |
| `#4051` | quota: the commit lane's only org-limit gate was the session cap | 1 (revenue guard) |
| `#10175` | ops(capture): the hosted capture cap is HELD deliberately — never override | 1 (standing rule, not work) |
| `#8486` | **Run LongMemEval-S** (never executed; no comparable number exists) | **4 — this IS the benchmark** |
| `#2513` | multi-session retrieval evidence surface — the dominant QA loss (53 % of misses) | **3** |
| `#8488` | context-enriched embeddings **+ BM25 lexical** — the two signals we lack | **3** |
| `#10538` | time-aware query expansion — the fix for the 53 %-of-misses part | **3** |
| `#2281` | ask/answer surface reads ingest-time-distilled knowledge (ontology-organised) with raw-turn fallback | **3** |
| `#9097` | measure(ask): seal and publish the Q3 exit measurement | **4 (it is a measurement)** |
| `#11460` | re-register the ask exit pre-registration to the owner-ruled DeepSeek judge | **4 (prerequisite of #9097)** |
| **`#4333`** | **storage-architecture owner** — node volume + true per-node cost. **`P2-moderate`, so it is deliberately OUTSIDE the beta set** (the set is P0/P1) and is listed here only so nobody re-files it as a `#5090` child: it is the *owner* of the storage question, not a child of the vector layer | **3 (not beta)** |
| `#11395` | tracking(5090): the S3 vector-removal / surface-approval call has no successor issue | **3** |
| `#10656` | **credential provenance (REOPENED 2026-11-11** — it had been closed COMPLETED by a PR that never touched it; all three claims re-measured true at `origin/main` `372f926cd9`: `:1506` writes `<cwd>/.tortoise`, `:2133` ranks it above the global store, `:1662-3` is a non-atomic `write_text`+`chmod`) — plaintext key in a working tree, at a precedence that shadows the user-global store. **Both halves are lane decisions, not owner ones** (contradiction test 2026-11-11: no recorded decision requires the cwd location — it arrived with `61f32e1ce4` and `#1708` moved `signup`/`recover` to the global store without ever ruling on `init`). (a) atomic write + FIFO guard **dispatched**; (c) write to the user-global store with `<cwd>/.tortoise` kept read-compatible **decided and queued behind (a)** — same function, so one lane at a time | 1 |
| `#11912` | **`doctor` cannot see half the product** — 8 local checks, **zero** credential or hosted ones, so a revoked key reads `8 pass, 0 fail` (measured on this box). #10655 built `config show` (the offline reporter); this is the first-run surface that should REACH it. **Dispatched** | 1 |
| `#12060` | **P1 NEW — per-kind guards: redirect mis-filed writes with an AX contract, not a refusal.** Every core kind gets a deterministic, token-free guard: accept / **redirect** / refuse — a guard may never refuse a case whose right home is known. Shipped with a fixed AX message shape (what changed, why, the exact override, how to undo) plus a `kind_redirect` field so agents branch on data not English, an `intent="as_declared"` override that records that it fired, and redirect counters. **Cross-pack resolved:** targets are core / own namespace / `depends_on` only; `pack validate` refuses a bad reference (fail at install, not at write); at write time a missing target makes the guard **abstain** — never reject, because a write must not depend on which packs are installed. Packs declare guards **optionally**; `_template` carries a worked example. **Prevents the re-file from re-creating the 453 issue-as-Subject + 870 `other` nodes** | 1 |

### ✅ DEFINITION — UNCHANGED, AND NOT MINE TO MOVE (owner, 2026-11-09)
> **"the cut line depends on what's needed not a fixed number — focus on advancing towards the private-beta while I handle what 'done' is and my definition hasn't changed."**

**So: beta ships when the open `P0-blocker` + `P1-severe` issues are merged and closed. There is no A/B/C, no relabelling, no frozen set.** The options previously written here are withdrawn — they were me asking the owner to solve a *queue-dynamics* problem that is the fleet's job to solve by closing issues.

**What that makes true immediately:**
- **The six P1s filed yesterday are BETA WORK, not a post-beta wave.** `#11641 #11642 #11646 #11653 #11654 #11656` join Stage 1 and get dispatched like any other beta item.
- **The P1 count rising is not an argument to narrow the definition — it is a dispatch backlog.** Report it as such: *N new beta items, N dispatched, N unassigned.*
- **Nothing is relabelled.** Recent additions to the set stay `P1-severe`; `#11382` is proposed for `P1-severe` and `#8713` already carries `P2-moderate`.

**Stage 3 is days, not weeks — because the fixes are already written and switched off.** So (A) costs little and keeps the beta definition intact. **Still the owner's word to confirm, and nothing has been relabelled.**

### ⛔ AND THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS MORE THAN ANY OF THE ABOVE: **P1 grew 17 → 22 today**
```
P0 open: 10 (unchanged)   P1 open: **17 → 22**   issues closed today: 27 — of which only **2 were P0/P1**
```

**"All P0/P1" is a moving target: the fleet is filing real Severe findings faster than it lands fixes.** That — not the size of any single wave — is the strongest reason to state an explicit **cut line** for the beta: a sha, a date, or a named issue set frozen at that moment. Otherwise the beta definition cannot be completed, only approached.

---

## STAGE 2 — ⏸ AFTER PRIVATE BETA, NOT IN IT: the venture-studio design partner

> **⛔ DO NOT LABEL `#2696` P0 OR P1 UNTIL THE PRIVATE-BETA SET IS COMPLETE, AND DO NOT DISPATCH IT.**
> The order is: **finish the private-beta set first.** A `P0`/`P1` label on this would make the automated harness pick it up and pull it into the beta wave — which is the opposite of the ruling. **It stays `P2-moderate`.** The ruling is: *"P2 for now, prioritise to P0 for the design partner after we complete the requirements for the private-beta"* (owner, 2026-11-09).
> **This section exists so the work is not lost, not so it is started.**

**The issue exists: `#2696` (currently `P2-moderate`) — "epic: meeting-ingestion pipeline for venture-builder customers — meeting-attunement".**
Its subject is exactly the partner's need: a meeting *is* a session, but its structure is different (speakers, agenda, decisions, action items, cross-meeting continuity) from an agent session's (tool calls, file edits, errors fixed).

**The question you raised — one universal extractor, or modular variants?** The evidence we have says **modularise the seam, keep one extractor**:
- The extractor is already staged S0→S6 (`#5087`) with a per-stage contract, and `#11484` derives the structural write vocabulary **per graph** from core + packs. That is already a per-domain configuration seam.
- A "meeting variant" that is a *prompt-and-vocabulary* variant costs little; a forked pipeline costs a second capstone and a second set of guarantees (verbatim retention `#10360`, value survival `#10989`).
- **So: one extractor, one proof, two profiles.** Stage 2's real work is (a) a meeting profile — speaker turns, decisions, action items — as a pack/vocabulary, and (b) the ingestion path from a transcript source to the extractor's door.

**This stage also carries `#2696` from P2 → the label that makes auto-dispatch pick it up *after* the beta set.** That relabel is part of the same decision as (A)/(B)/(C) above.

**⚠️ Prerequisite for iterating the profile at all — `#11661` (`P2-moderate`, deliberately NOT a beta item).** We record *which source version* produced a fact and never *which extractor* did, so after a profile change there is no way to tell which already-ingested meetings need re-extraction: every tuning round either re-extracts the whole corpus or silently serves output from a prompt that no longer exists, and neither failure is visible in the graph. Filed with its design — `extractorId` (a deliberately-bumped profile identity) + `extractorDigest` (a hash of the compiled prompt/vocabulary, for explainability), carried on the `extractedFrom` link exactly as `sourceVersion` already is, plus a third `unknown` state so pre-existing nodes are neither blessed as fresh nor re-extracted wholesale. **Do not pull it into the private-beta wave** — it is not a launch requirement. **Promote it to `P1` at the moment meeting-profile iteration starts**, because that is when its absence stops being a nuisance and becomes a correctness risk (`D13` draft → run → look → refine is the working method, so iteration starts immediately after stage 2 begins).

**The decision itself is recorded on `#2696` (comment `6752567775`) and `#11081` (`6752174448`, corrected by `6752335134`):** one extractor, no fork, meetings as connector #4 conforming to the registry-free mapper contract; the profile is a **shape** mapping (speaker turn · section · action item · decision · status update · blocker · open question), not a source-branded prompt set; no depth/cheap mode; no per-source field-cost registry.

## STAGE 3 — THE LONG-MEMORY FIXES THE BENCHMARK WOULD OTHERWISE MEASURE AS BROKEN

**The organising rule for this stage, and it is the whole point of it:** *an issue whose build landed is not done — it is at the "decide, or experiment and decide from the results" step.* **Building a retrieval improvement, leaving it switched off, and abandoning it is the worst outcome, and it is the current state of two of these.** Every row below therefore names its **decision home** and its **next action**, not just its subject.

**They may be re-prioritised to `P1` once the private-beta set is complete**, if the owner then decides they are needed. Until that point a `P1` label on any of them would make the automated harness pull it into the beta wave — which is exactly what Stage 2's `⛔ DO NOT LABEL` rule exists to prevent for `#2696`. **Leave them `P2`; re-prioritise after beta, not before.**

**These are the ones we already know are broken and know how they are broken.** Running LongMemEval before them measures our own known defects.

## STAGE 4 — THE BENCHMARKS
| what | issue | state |
|---|---|---|
| LongMemEval-S (end-to-end QA) | `#8486` | **never executed** — no comparable number exists |
| the ask exit measurement | `#9097` (+ `#11460` re-registration) | pre-registration owed |
| **reasoning (gbrain)** | `#1402` epic agent-reasoning eval battery · `#2080` epic gbrain learnings · `#2107` capstone | partially set up |
| battery wiring | `#2800`, `#11056` | in progress |

**Rule for this stage: a benchmark result is only published with (a) the sha, (b) the corpus hash, and (c) the profile/config it ran under.** A number without those three is not a measurement.

---

## Working rules (learned the hard way; all measured)

- **One lane per item; the terminal milestone is LANDED + CLOSED**, not "a PR opened".
- **Closure requires proven criteria** — a closing keyword only when the last criterion is proven beside the measurement.
- **A review lane records at the FINAL head.** Push first, then review, then record, then **read back** `~/.pi/agent/reviews/…json` and assert `head_sha` matches. A record bound to a stale sha is indistinguishable from no record — three died that way on 2026-11-09.
- **`mergeable` AND `mergeStateStatus` are both caches.** `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <head>` is the only authority; acting on a phantom `DIRTY` moves heads and destroys reviews.
- **Never edit a PR body after a review is recorded** — it wipes the attestation.
- **Never push to a PR whose CI is queued or running** — it cancels that run.
- **Pre-flight before dispatch**: `collision_preflight.py <N>` + `who-is-on.sh <N>`.
- **Keep advanced work.** Adopt and drive existing work to completion; re-do only where it is genuinely off, and file a follow-up rather than starting over silently.

## Instruments (do not re-derive)
`~/.pi/agent/state/P01-PRMAP.md` · `~/.pi/agent/state/WORKSTATUS.md` · `uv run python tools/surface-target-check.py` · `tools/surface_manifest.py check` · the `tracking-table` comment this issue carries (posted every beat).

Any advice would be appreciated.

### What happened/what did you expect to happen?

We have set our Argo Workflows with `parallelism: 2048` and `- --qps=2048`. We have no `namespaceParallelism`. We are also running 5 Workflow Controllers. The system runs up to 3000 workflows during the day in 2 different namespaces. However, we have noticed that we end up having a lot of Pending workflows with the message: `Workflow processing has been postponed because too many workflows are already running` while there are 0 `Running` workflows at that very moment, and 2000+ workflows marked as `Succeeded`. Our default TTL for workflows is 24h but we did add some in the last week that have a longer TTL - 3-4 days for some jobs.

The moment I manually delete all the `Succeeded` workflows using `kubectl delete wf -n argo -l workflows.argoproj.io/phase=Succeeded` the workflows get unclogged and everything runs as normal. While it is not a problem to lower the TTL for successful jobs I am wondering if this is intended behaviour or if we are missing something in our configuration. I have read the whole default `values.yaml` in the Helm chart for Argo Worfklows but I didn't see anything pointing to this particular issue.
